added.summary: The play surface presents the widest gamut and range the surface and display offer: extended range (HDR) with Display P3 on Metal (scRGB EDR), DX12 and Vulkan (scRGB), and WebGPU (a `display-p3` canvas with `toneMapping: extended`), else Display P3 at standard range, else sRGB. `wide` keeps standard range, `srgb` the output as before. Offscreen renderers, captures and reference frames stay sRGB at standard range.
Whether the surface presents Display P3; `hdr` whether it presents extended range.

On an extended-range output ACES, AgX, Khronos PBR Neutral and none keep middle grey where SDR puts it and end at the headroom (RenderOptions.peakNits over paperWhiteNits, 1000 / 203 left out, no more than the display reports) instead of SDR white: emissive, glow, bloom and the sun keep rising past white.

added.member: UI: Display P3 colours and the display media queries
added.summary: On a Display P3 output, CSS colours outside sRGB (`color(display-p3 …)`, a wide `oklch()`, a mix of them) keep their gamut, gamut mapped into P3 by OKLCh chroma reduction instead of into sRGB. `(color-gamut: p3)` and `(dynamic-range: high)` (and `video-dynamic-range`) match where the surface presents them; they were fixed false.

breaking.change: Removed: HDR is no longer opt-in. RenderOptions.output (left out `best`) presents extended range and Display P3 wherever the surface offers them, and the tone curve the game chose extends to the headroom instead of the LPM mapper replacing it. On an SDR display or surface nothing changes.
breaking.fix: Delete `hdr: true`. To keep a game at SDR on HDR displays, set `render: { output: "wide" }` (Display P3, standard range) or `output: "srgb"` in GameDesc.
